title: Asking for Help in Another Language

lessons.title: つうやく (tsūyaku) — interpreting; an interpreter

segments.text: Before the new one: say the Japanese for to search all over, then the Japanese for fortunately.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: つうやく

segments.text: つうやく — tsūyaku — "interpreting; an interpreter".
がいこくで あにが つうやくを しました。 — gaikoku de ani ga tsūyaku o shimashita — "Abroad, my brother did the interpreting."

つうやく (tsūyaku) is Sino-Japanese (kango): two Chinese characters read with their on'yomi, readings borrowed from Chinese. They are tsū, "pass through" (Middle Chinese thuwng) and yaku, "translate" (yek) (KANJIDIC2; Middle Chinese in Baxter's transcription).
One more word for getting around.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: ほんやく

segments.text: ほんやく — hon'yaku — "translation (of writing)".
この てがみの ほんやくを おねがいします。 — kono tegami no hon'yaku o onegai shimasu — "Please translate this letter for me."

ほんやく (hon'yaku) is Sino-Japanese (kango): two Chinese characters read with their on'yomi, readings borrowed from Chinese. They are hon, "turn over" (Middle Chinese phjon) and yaku, "translate" (yek) (KANJIDIC2; Middle Chinese in Baxter's transcription).

lessons.title: といあわせる (toiawaseru) — to make an enquiry

segments.text: Before the new one: say the Japanese for interpreting, then the Japanese for translation.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: といあわせる

segments.text: といあわせる — toiawaseru — "to make an enquiry".
でんわで えきに といあわせました。 — denwa de eki ni toiawasemashita — "I phoned the station to ask."
Polite といあわせます, toiawasemasu; an ichidan verb. Past (polite): ちちが りょかんに といあわせました。, chichi ga ryokan ni toiawasemashita.

といあわせる (toiawaseru) is a native Japanese word (wago), inherited rather than borrowed from Chinese, built from toi, "asking" (from tou) and awaseru, "to bring together"; its kanji were attached later as kun'yomi (JMdict).
One more word for getting around.

lessons.title: つうじる (tsūjiru) — to be understood; to get through
lessons.gloss: to be understood; to get through

segments.text: Before the new one: say the Japanese for translation, then the Japanese for to make an enquiry.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: つうじる

segments.text: つうじる — tsūjiru — "to be understood; to get through".
日本語が つうじて、あんしんしました。 — nihongo ga tsūjite, anshin shimashita — "I was relieved that my Japanese was understood."
Polite つうじます, tsūjimasu; an ichidan verb. Past (polite): あにの 日本語が つうじました。, ani no nihongo ga tsūjimashita.

つうじる (tsūjiru) is built from both layers of the vocabulary: the Sino-Japanese tsū, "pass through" (Middle Chinese thuwng), an on'yomi borrowed from Chinese, made into a verb with the native ending -jiru, a form of suru, "to do", inherited rather than borrowed (JMdict; KANJIDIC2; Middle Chinese in Baxter's transcription).
One more word for getting around.

lessons.title: じゅうでん (jūden) — charging a battery; recharging

segments.text: Before the new one: say the Japanese for to make an enquiry, then the Japanese for to be understood.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: じゅうでん

segments.text: じゅうでん — jūden — "charging a battery; recharging".
えきで でんわを じゅうでんしました。 — eki de denwa o jūden shimashita — "I charged my phone at the station."

じゅうでん (jūden) is Sino-Japanese (kango): two Chinese characters read with their on'yomi, readings borrowed from Chinese. They are jū, "fill" (Middle Chinese tsyhuwng) and den, "electricity" (denH) (KANJIDIC2; Middle Chinese in Baxter's transcription).
